title: Dispatch TUR 6: City Bars Work at the Unbuilt Terminus
summary: A new letter says the children can hear Alderwick debating their rescue.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The council voted six to three against construction beneath the goods depot last night. Alderman Dorne said no engineer could certify a platform intended for a train that has no physical track. He also cited three reports of water appearing on cellar floors along the old Westmere route.

Within an hour of the vote, Mr. Pike received a letter dated 17 October 1894. Its writer, Miriam Harrow, says the passengers listened through the guard’s speaking tube as voices from Alderwick argued about whether to let them arrive. She does not describe how those voices reached a train in the marsh.

“Mama says she will come,” the letter reads. Mrs. Harrow confirmed that she said as much on the council steps before the vote. She had not yet spoken to Mr. Pike. The child’s words appear on paper that was in his locked office when the council convened.

Dr. Saye now believes the line connects a future journey to Alderwick’s present, rather than delivering mail from one date to another by ordinary post. The train’s arrival, if there is one, may occur on the date the terminus is made ready. She cannot predict what will happen to passengers who were born after that date.

Mr. Wren has begun drawing a freestanding platform that can be assembled above ground, with a clock, three red lamps, and a painted station name. He says the city can forbid excavation. It cannot forbid a carpenter from building a place to stand.
